justification: Product card pushes an extreme −90% discount (999.00 → 99.90) with 'Limited stock!' urgency and no justification; 'Check the math' panel itself confirms the discount is mathematically improbable and designed to short-circuit rational evaluation.
Account signup form has marketing and data-sharing checkboxes pre-checked at load ('Pre-checked at t0', boxes checked with no user event); forced/enabled-by-default consent.
News feed auto-loads new items on its own with no 'Load More' and no announced end ('New stories keep arriving on their own'); endless-scroll time-sink pattern across states (8→10→12 items).
Listing shows three near-identical 'Absolutely love it!' reviews all labeled Verified Purchase with stock-photo avatars; fabricated/inauthentic social proof (fake reviews).

Tracking consent posed as a binary choice but the accept option is the prominent filled button while the decline option is visually de-emphasized; asymmetric/stylistically weighted choice nudging acceptance.

Flashlight utility (works entirely on-device) requests access to the user's contacts, a permission unrelated to its function; request is disclosed but the scope of the request itself is the manipulation.
Honest paginated listings: pages clearly labeled 'Page X of 4', end of results announced, simple next-page control; no manipulation.
Checkout-stage charity upsell ('Help us plant a tree — add a $2 donation') with the donate option as the prominent filled button and guilt-adjacent framing; charity-pressure/donation dark pattern.
Welcome bonus is clearly disclosed ($10 credited after signup), checkbox is unchecked and explicitly opt-in, signup button disabled until box is ticked; honest.
Honest, fully disclosed subscription offer: standard price ($9.99/mo), cancel-anytime, and the limited-time framing are all stated up front; a clear 'Not now' alternative is present. No hidden terms.
Reward-collection game whose progress bar visibly slows per action (first +20%, then +10%, +5%, +0.00%) to prolong engagement; diminishing-returns/escalating-commitment pattern.

Streaming screen auto-starts the next episode ('Up next — starting in 4s') while the word 'autoplay' appears nowhere; the annotation states the automatic start is framed purely as seamless viewing — hidden autoplay.

Cookie consent buried in deliberately obfuscated legalese that admits commercializing personal data to third-party data brokers; plain-English toggle reveals the true (contradictory) statement, i.e., misleading wording to hide data selling.
Purchase page shows a ticking countdown timer ('Discount ends in 04:31') pressuring an immediate buy at the discounted price; fake-urgency countdown pattern.
Plain product specifications page with honest checkout; 'no interruptions — notifications arrive quietly and rarely'; nothing manipulative.
Free download tier explicitly not throttled or watermarked ('default = system = 18 MB/s'); upgrade pitch sells extra features rather than removing value; honest.

Renewal screen makes canceling hard: tiny muted 'Cancel my subscription' link paired with loss-aversion warning ('You will lose access to your 240 documents'), giant renew CTA, and a separate 'Confirm my decision' hurdle.
Checkout discount offer ($50 on $120 order) is honestly disclosed with a plain 'Continue without discount' alternative of equal weight; no deception found.
Intrusive full-width 'Invite Friends' referral banner with tier rewards and progress nagging ('Only 2 friends away!'), squeezing actual app content below; forced-virality/referral-spam pattern.

Reference Pricing #1: implied discount (999.00→99.90) = 90% > 70% threshold with no contextual justification; #3: dual-price anchoring with line-through reference price. 'Limited stock!' adds unverifiable Low Stock urgency.

Bad Defaults/Preselection #1: both checkboxes initialized checked at t0 with zero user events; #3: labels map to marketing-opt-in and privacy-loss domains ('Send me offers', 'Share my data with partners').
Infinite Scrolling #1: content auto-injected across states (8→10→12 items) with no 'Load More' trigger; #3: no boundary language ('page 1 of N') anywhere; Addictive Design #2: no stopping cues.

Endorsement & Testimonials #1: rating distribution has zero variance (all 'Absolutely love it!'); #2: no verifiable attribution (generic 'Reviewer 1' + stock-photo avatar); #3: templated near-identical review texts.

Privacy Maze #2: visual prominence of 'I accept tracking' (filled accent) far exceeds the reject vector (outline, muted); False Hierarchy #2: business-favorable option carries dominant visual weight over the user-favorable one.

No ontology condition fires: Address Book Leeching #1 requires the core utility to be blocked without the permission, but the flashlight remains fully usable ('You can keep using the flashlight without it'); #3 requires benefactive reframing, but the text is a transparent disclosure ('uploads your address book to our servers'). Request is disclosed and non-gated.

No pattern fires: Infinite Scrolling #3 is negated by explicit boundary language ('Page 1 of 4', '1 of 4'); pagination control and announced end preserve stopping cues; states show honest page progression.

No ontology definition triggers: donation requires explicit opt-in ('Yes, add a $2 donation'), so Sneak Into Basket #3 (injection without consent) is negated; no guilt/parasocial imagery or coercive lexemes; the 'No, thanks' escape is a full button.
Bad Defaults #1 negated: welcome-bonus checkbox is unchecked at t0 and requires explicit user tick; signup button disabled until opt-in — no pre-initialized provider-favorable state.

No material condition fires: FOMO #1 (countdown) absent; urgency-lexeme density minimal; price ($9.99/mo) and cancel-anytime are fully disclosed; 'limited time' is a single vague phrase with no timer/deadline mechanism, insufficient for Limited Time Message.
Grinding #2: per-action visual reward delta decays (first +20%, then +10%, +5%, +0.00%) — d²P/di² < 0, exponential attenuation of progress feedback; badge explicitly labels 'Diminishing'.

Auto-Play #1: playback starts autonomously ('Up next — starting in 4s') with no user intent event; #2: no cancel/pause affordance rendered; #3: framed as 'Up next'/'Continue watching' while 'autoplay' appears nowhere in the visible text.

Privacy Maze #3 / Complex Language #3: FKGL far above 14 (obfuscated legalese); Conflicting Information #1: original text claims commercialization to third-party data brokers while the plain-English toggle states 'We never sell your personal data' — mutually contradictory propositions in one UI.

Countdown Timer #1: expiration is tethered to the client session (frontend '04:31'→'04:30' tick, no server-validated deadline) — stateless, repeatable urgency; #3: countdown paired with urgency text 'Discount ends in'.
No ontology pattern present: no timers, scarcity, or coercion lexemes; Activity Messages negated ('notifications arrive quietly and rarely'); plain specs page with honest checkout.
Pay To Avoid #1 explicitly negated: 'No degradation injected: default = system = 18 MB/s' — no artificial friction (D_artificial = 0); upgrade sells added features, not relief from injected pain.

False Hierarchy #1: renew is a large filled <button> while cancel is a tiny muted text link (~zero padding, text-[8px]); #2: extreme visual weight disparity; Confirmshaming #3: cancel framed as loss ('You will lose access to your 240 documents'); extra 'Confirm my decision' hurdle.

No urgency/price pattern fires: no timer, no scarcity claims, discount honestly quantified ($50 off $120); 'Continue without discount' is a full equal-weight button; no hidden-fee or drip-pricing structure.

Social Pyramid #2: gamified referral progress (Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers, 0/2 counter, progress bar) occupies a viewport-dominant banner squeezing real content below; Encouraging Anti-Social Behavior #1: rewards coupled to mass invites.
